question: Can the previously successful fixed-grid history interface learn three consecutive swaps when supervised at every swap endpoint, without action loss?

controlled_architecture.readout: one shared IntegratedCurrentReadout used for all three endpoints

endpoint_construction.swap_0: frames 0..29 followed by frame 29 repeated through position 59
endpoint_construction.swap_1: frames 0..39 followed by frame 39 repeated through position 59
endpoint_construction.swap_2: frames 0..49 followed by frame 49 repeated through position 59
endpoint_construction.reason_for_padding: keep the production fixed 60-position interface while preventing future-frame leakage
endpoint_construction.joint_objective: three shared 3-way logits factorized into one 27-way joint distribution; cross entropy equals the sum of the three endpoint cross entropies

phase_readout_only.description: freeze the existing history encoder and train only the shared endpoint readout

phase_joint_aux.description: initialize from readout_only, then train the same shared history encoder and shared readout with endpoint classification only

conclusion: The input, labels, optimizer path, and gradients are functional because swap_0 reaches 99.83% validation accuracy.
A frozen encoder exposes strong swap_0 information but nearly random swap_1 and swap_2 information, so the old final-only representation did not preserve a reusable three-swap state.

Dense endpoint supervision improves swap_1 only modestly and does not improve swap_2; the depth-2 one-shot non-causal aggregation learns the first segment far more easily than a rule that is repeatedly applied across all three swaps.

This result argues against classifier initialization or the final readout as the principal bottleneck. The next architecture test should add segment-wise or recurrent state updates with shared weights, then reuse this same endpoint evaluation unchanged.
